subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures remain accepted asynchronously and terminalize with a typed failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight enough Docker startup work to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: The repair shape affects the public async spawn contract, registry state, gateway wait/session projections, and the overlapping startup lifecycle tracker, so automation should not pick the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagent list, and agent wait.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move Docker startup validation before acceptance and reject immediately, accepting extra latency and compatibility implications.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue as the sandbox-specific repro while resolving the broader startup lifecycle direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagent list, and agent wait.

likelyOwner.reason: The symbol history ties Peter to the original `sessions_spawn` contract plus cross-agent/sandbox follow-up work, making him the best available owner for the API/behavior choice.
